package_info.package_name: Multiple (see list in report, e.g., 1inch, 4ff-lib-foundation, @malware-test-bises-celts-borel-sneak/test-mlw3-bises-celts-borel-sneak, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were flagged as malicious, suspicious, or involved in dependency confusion attacks by Sonatype's automated malware detection system. The macro-level reasoning is that these packages are either intentionally crafted to perform malicious actions, mimic legitimate packages (typosquatting), or are part of supply chain attacks targeting open source ecosystems.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual or unauthorized network requests during install or import
Access to sensitive files or environment variables at install/import/runtime
Typosquatting or name similarity to popular packages
Unexpected script execution in package lifecycle hooks (e.g., postinstall)
file_indicators: Presence of install scripts (e.g., postinstall in package.json, setup.py with exec calls)
Files with obfuscated or minified code in unexpected locations
Unusual or duplicate package names mimicking popular libraries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during install/import
HTTP/S requests to webhook, pastebin, or exfiltration endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting), analyze package install and import scripts for unauthorized network or file access, and flag any package that attempts to exfiltrate data or execute code during installation or import. Use automated behavioral analysis to quarantine suspicious packages for manual review before allowing them into the build pipeline.
